strengths: Automatically discovering the vocabulary addresses a useful limitation of open-vocabulary segmentation. AutoSeg offers a modular approach using pretrained models without additional model training.
Captioning clustered subsets of BLIP patch embeddings is an interesting technical contribution that plausibly improves coverage of less salient objects.

The experiments provide encouraging evidence for local captioning. Table 1 improves class-agnostic IoU over plain BLIP plus X-Decoder across all four datasets. With the same segmentor, Table 4 reports VOC mIoU of 87.1 versus 56.7 for LLaVA and 41.1 for SAM plus BLIP.

The pipeline is clearly illustrated, reused models and datasets are identified, and implementation settings are provided. Supplementary failure cases usefully expose compound-noun errors and competition between related labels.
weaknesses: LAVE, on which the main quantitative conclusions depend, lacks validation against human-verified mappings or analysis of sensitivity to the LLM and prompts. Appendix A relies on the LLM remembering the Context and ADE20K vocabularies instead of supplying them. Its prompts also map stuff terms to background despite these datasets containing annotated stuff categories; the exact-match override in Algorithm 1 does not resolve this for synonyms. These choices can materially distort evaluation.

Table 3 needs reconciliation of benchmark protocols. Context scores such as 65.1 for X-Decoder and 58.4 for FC-CLIP appear to correspond to PC-59, although the column is labeled PC-459. Furthermore, ZeroSeg uses a different semantic mapping procedure, and the manuscript does not establish that its predictions were reevaluated with LAVE. The superiority claims therefore lack a clearly comparable evaluation.

Model selection is insufficiently separated from evaluation. Section 4.1 describes Bayesian optimization against VOC mIoU without identifying a disjoint tuning split, and Table 3 adopts each dataset’s best caption-cycle setting from Table 2. Independent evaluation and repeated runs are needed, particularly because caption generation is stochastic and the reported Context advantage is only 0.3 points.

The ablations establish the usefulness of the complete pipeline but do not isolate multiscale processing, cluster alignment, positional features, CRF refinement, or majority filtering. Consequently, the necessity of the proposed clustering machinery remains uncertain. Runtime measurements would also clarify the cost of repeated caption decoding.

Mapped benchmark mIoU does not establish the correctness of the newly generated, fine-grained categories: erroneous names can collapse to the same dataset label or background. The central claim of accurate recognition beyond dataset vocabularies needs systematic assessment beyond selected qualitative examples.

Secondary reproducibility issues remain: Equation 9 specifies independent maximum-IoU assignments rather than the stated Hungarian matching, and the handling of different-resolution cluster grids and additional positional dimensions before frozen BLIP decoding is unclear.
